{"id":"0af6061e-8f51-4bdf-afa2-454faacd86aa","object":"chat.completion","created":1790510290,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"type":"json_object","parent_requirement_id":"R3","mode":"probe","used_claims":[],"local_residual":"Whether the artist’s partner at the time of the artist’s death gave an interview in which they said that, following the artist’s death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of the artist’s songs."}","reasoning_content":"We need answer JSON only. Need identify one coherent local residual inside parent requirement R3. We have original question, parent requirement: "The partner of the artist (at the time of their death) gave an interview where they said that following their death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." Current claims: C1 Sophie died in Athens? Actually says Sophie died aged 34 on 30 Jan 2021 after accidental fall while watching full moon; accident in Athens, Greece. Parent requirement concerns partner interview statement. Need choose one residual objective. Are there any verified claims supporting R3? C1 identifies artist? It doesn't mention partner or interview. So no substantive supporting Claim for R3. Thus mode probe, used_claims []. local_residual should be exploratory evidence objective, not search query. Need preserve participant roles etc. We need ask to establish that a partner of the artist (at time of death) gave an interview, or maybe the relation "partner said after death artist became direct reference to one of their songs". Since no support, choose one coherent facet. Could be "Whether the artist's partner at the time of the artist's death gave an interview in which they made a statement about the artist becoming a direct reference to one of the artist's songs." That's the whole parent requirement? But one coherent evidence objective can be the existence of such an interview/partner statement. Need maybe not bundle independent? The parent requirement has multiple conditions: partner at time of death, gave interview, said after death artist has become direct reference to one of their songs. We can choose one local residual: identify/confirm the partner's interview statement connecting the artist's death to a song. But if no verified claim, one exploratory facet: "Whether there is a partner of the artist at the time of the artist's death who gave an interview containing the statement that after the artist's death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." That's entire condition. Is that allowed? It's one coherent evidence objective. Could be considered bundling interview and statement but they are one relation. The instruction: If no substantive part supported, choose one faithful low-commitment facet. Maybe better: "Whether the artist had a partner at the time of their death who gave an interview about the artist's posthumous reference to one of the artist's songs." That includes partner. But need preserve uncertainty. Since C1 is about Sophie; we don't know if artist is Sophie? Actually Original Question refers to "A musical artist..." Current claim C1 likely from research about artist. Parent requirement R3 says "The partner of the artist..." We don't know if artist = Sophie? C1 says Sophie died. It may be relevant but not established that Sophie is the target artist? In the context, likely C1 is about the artist. But no claim explicitly linking Sophie to parent requirement. For R3, used_claims? If C1 supports death details but not R3. The instruction: Only Verified Claims count as established evidence. If some part of Parent Requirement already established by Claims, do not ask. C1 doesn't support partner interview. So used_claims [].

Need output JSON exactly with mode "probe", used_claims [].

local_residual: Must be evidence objective, not query. Avoid adding outside knowledge. Could say: "Whether the artist’s partner at the time of the artist’s death gave an interview in which they stated that following the artist’s death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of the artist’s songs." This is the full R3. But if no part supported, it's okay? The instruction says if no substantive part supported, still choose one faithful low-commitment facet. The facet could be the existence of the interview statement. That might be the entire requirement, but it's a single coherent evidence objective. However maybe we should narrow to "whether there exists an interview by the artist's partner at the time of death" rather than the song-reference content. But the parent requirement includes the statement. If we only establish interview existence, we don't establish statement. But local residual should be one coherent part. The question's target is song title. The parent requirement is the interview statement. The key residual is the content of the partner's statement linking death to song. Maybe ask: "Whether the artist’s partner at the time of death said in an interview that the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs following the artist’s death." That's the core.

Maybe include artist identity? "For the artist identified in C1 (Sophie), whether the partner at the time of death gave an interview stating that following the artist's death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of their songs." But used_claims would then include C1? We are using C1 to identify artist? The schema: used_claims are claims used to establish residual. If we mention Sophie, we rely on C1 for artist identity. But R3 doesn't mention Sophie; C1 gives death info. Is it okay to use C1? The instruction: If input contains no substantive supporting Claim, use mode probe and used_claims []. But C1 is substantive supporting? It supports death context but not parent requirement. It may be supporting for identifying artist but not R3. The mode depends on supporting Claim for the Parent Requirement. Since no claim directly supports R3, I'd use probe and [].

But could we use C1 as context to anchor artist? The parent requirement says "the artist". We can phrase without naming: "Whether the artist’s partner at the time of the artist’s death gave an interview in which they said that, following the artist’s death, the artist has become a direct reference to one of the artist’s songs." That preserves.

Need ensure JSON valid. Only JSON object. No markdown.
